title_ar: الشيخ الددو يحاضر لجمعية المرأة عن محبة المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures to the Women's Association on Love of the Chosen One, upon him be blessings and peace
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة الشيخ العلامة محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء محاضرة بدار الشباب القديمة مساء أمس الأربعاء 16 ربيع الأول 1433هـ الموافق: 2012/02/08 تحت عنوان: "على محبة المصطفى نلتقي" بدعوة وتنظيم من جمعية المرأة للتربية والثقافة. وقد تحدث الشيخ في محاضرته عن شمائل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأسباب محبته وذكر أنها تجتمع في خمسة أمور ينبغي تحصيلها عند كل مسلم لكي تتحقق له محبته صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهي: 1-الجمال؛ فكل جميل محبوب والنبي (ص) أجمل الناس وأكرمهم. 2-التخلق بأخلاقه صلى الله عليه وسلم. 3-إحسانه في معاملاته. 4- الرجاء؛ وهو رجاء الفوز في الآخرة ومشاهدها. 5- العلاقة؛ ومن أعظمها علاقة النبي (ص) بأمته وتعلقها به وبالفوز في الآخرة بجميع تجلياته. كما تطرق الشيخ - حفظه الله - في حديثه لمجمل جوانب محبته عليه الصلاة والسلام، وما وصفه به الشعراء والبلغاء من العرب الأقدمين من جمال خَلق ودماثة خُلق. وقد ذكر الشيخ أمثلة رائعة من تمام صفحه وكرمه وشجاعته وفروسيته وطيبه عليه الصلاة والسلام، وملاطفته وعطفه على الصبيان، وإحسانه لنسائه أمهات المؤمنين والصغار من أهل بيته.. واستطرد لذلك الكثير من المواقف البارزة في سيرة المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام. وقد حضرت حشود جماهيرية كثيرة من مختلف مشارب المجتمع، وأغلبها نسائي، واكتظت مدارج القاعة وممراتها بالجمهور.
body_en:
The eminent scholar Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a lecture at the Old Youth House on the evening of yesterday, Wednesday 16 Rabi' al-Awwal 1433 AH, corresponding to 08/02/2012, under the title "Upon Love of the Chosen One We Meet", at the invitation of and organised by the Women's Association for Upbringing and Culture.

In his lecture the Sheikh spoke of the noble qualities (shamāʾil) of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and of the causes of love for him, and he said that they come together in five things which every Muslim ought to acquire in order that love of him, may God bless him and grant him peace, be realised for him. They are: 1. Beauty — for everything beautiful is loved, and the Prophet (ṣ) was the most beautiful of people and the most noble of them. 2. Taking on his character, may God bless him and grant him peace. 3. His excellence in his dealings with others. 4. Hope — that is, the hope of success in the hereafter and of its scenes. 5. Connection — and among the greatest of these is the Prophet's (ṣ) connection with his community, and its attachment to him and to success in the hereafter in all its manifestations.

The Sheikh, may God preserve him, also addressed in his talk the aspects of love for him, upon him be blessings and peace, taken as a whole, and what the poets and the eloquent among the ancient Arabs described him with, of beauty of form and gentleness of character. The Sheikh mentioned splendid examples of the completeness of his forbearance, his generosity, his courage, his horsemanship and his sweetness, upon him be blessings and peace; of his gentleness and tenderness towards young boys; and of his excellent treatment of his wives, the Mothers of the Believers, and of the young of his household. He digressed in that connection to many of the notable episodes in the biography (sīrah) of the Chosen One, upon him be blessings and peace.

Large crowds attended from every walk of society, most of them women, and the tiers and passages of the hall were packed with the audience.

flags.context: أمثلة رائعة من تمام صفحه وكرمه وشجاعته وفروسيته وطيبه
flags.note: ṭīb in a list of the Prophet's shamāʾil most often means the fragrance of his person, a standard topic of that literature and a natural companion to the physical qualities listed beside it; but ṭīb also carries the general sense of goodness or pleasantness, and a news summary gives no context to decide. 'Sweetness' is used because it is ambiguous in the same way the Arabic is. Should be resolved against the recording.

flags.context: the third of the five causes of love for the Prophet
options: his excellence in his dealings with others
flags.note: HOMONYM WARNING. muʿāmalāt is carried in the glossary as 'transactions', the fiqh chapter on contracts and commerce. That sense is wrong here: the item sits in a list of the Prophet's personal qualities and means his conduct towards people generally. The glossary rendering has deliberately not been used.

flags.arabic: خمسة أمور ينبغي تحصيلها عند كل مسلم
flags.context: the five causes of love for the Prophet, as summarised by the news desk
options: render the five as the report gives them, with the report's compression visible
render as the Sheikh's own five-part teaching
flags.note: The five items are the news desk's compression of a lecture; items 1, 4 and 5 in particular are headings of one or two words with no explanation, and item 5 ('Connection') is barely intelligible as it stands. ينبغي is rendered 'ought to' and deliberately not mapped to any of the five rulings: it is the reporter's word, not a graded ruling by the Sheikh, and nothing in the record grades anything. Must be displayed as a news summary.

flags.note: The source abbreviates the prayer upon the Prophet in two places and writes it in full elsewhere in the same paragraph. The inconsistency is the source's; the English preserves it rather than normalising, because the corpus is being built as a record of what the site published.

translator_notes: A news-desk report, not a text by the Sheikh.
The CMS timestamp, 9 February 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the body dates the lecture to the evening of Wednesday 16 Rabi' al-Awwal 1433 / 8 February 2012.

جمال خَلق ودماثة خُلق is a rhymed pair in Arabic turning on the two vowellings of the same consonants (khalq, form; khuluq, character). The rhyme is not reproducible in English and has not been forced; the source's own vowel marks are preserved in body_ar.
